title: THREAT Matrix Framework Schema
description: JSON Schema for the THREAT Matrix framework.json canonical artifact. THREAT Matrix is an AI-native operational ontology for physical threat actor behavior. The schema is the public contract for consumers (RAG systems, AI agents, downstream security tooling). Field values must describe a property of the indicator/tactic type, not of any specific case or assessment. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles" for the full rule.

version.description: Semantic version of the framework content release.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. Increments on schema-breaking or schema-additive changes.

matrices.description: Four target matrices: person, facility, organization, infrastructure. Each matrix contains tactics and a scope sentence describing the primary threat actor objective that places a tactic in that matrix. The matrices container also carries a boundary_rule describing the framework-vs-operational partition principle. Since V1.6 each matrix is validated by its own per-matrix subschema: a matrix's tactics must carry that matrix's id prefix (TM/TF/TO/TI) AND a matrix field const-equal to the containing key, so a person tactic given a TF id or a matrix:'facility' field is rejected by schema alone.

boundary_rule.description: Framework-vs-operational boundary principle governing matrix placement. Authoring-time: one matrix per tactic, set by the threat actor's primary objective. Operational-time: real incidents may invoke tactics from multiple matrices via Detection Mesh cross-references (correlates_with at the indicator level). Type-level statement of the framework's organizing principle.

escalation_rubric.description: Framework-published recommendation for deriving escalation_weight from escalation_axes and mapping to severity_band. Type-level reference; consumers may follow or override with documented rationale. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

composite_math.description: Recommended formula for deriving escalation_weight from escalation_axes. Multiplicative across axes is the default; weighted-additive variants are acceptable when documented.

severity_thresholds.description: Numeric thresholds mapping escalation_weight to severity_band buckets.

severity_floor_rule.description: V1.3 triage-floor rule: behaviors applying direct physical force to a person carry a severity_floor that forces severity_band to at least that value regardless of computed weight.

detectability_guidance.description: Reading guidance for the detectability axis (rubric v1.2.0 flip and aftermath handling).

blast_radius_guidance.description: Reading guidance and method-collateral base rates for the blast_radius_potential axis.

method_collateral_base_rates.description: Per-method typical collateral base rates (0.0-10.0). note is prose; the remaining keys are numeric base rates.

axis_confidence_rubric.description: Derivation rules and level semantics for the per-axis axis_confidence marker (Ruling 10-A).

calibration_guidance.description: Type-level framework guidance on calibrating severity_thresholds to a consumer's threat-posture environment. The framework's default thresholds reflect the rubric v1.2.0 recalibration (medium/high keep the equal-quartile cuts; critical lowered from 7.5 to 6.5 against the realized scored population); consumers operating in higher-threat-posture environments (critical infrastructure, executive protection, dignitary protection) should shift `high` and `critical` thresholds downward to surface medium-weight indicators earlier in triage. Lower-posture environments may shift them upward. Document any deviation per CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

operations.description: Operations / scenarios composer (V5+). Real data is an empty array; will become a populated structure in V5 (the type will widen to object then).

ai_architecture.description: AI capability vectors and amplification risk metadata.

bibliography.description: Central citation library. Each key is a unique reference ID; each value is a bibliographic entry.

phase_mappings.description: Cross-walk from THREAT Matrix phases to NTAC, Calhoun-Weston, CERT, Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK, and MITRE ATLAS stages. Enables AI/RAG cross-framework interoperability across physical, cyber, and AI-systems threat actor models.

detection_mesh.description: Architectural prose object describing the cross-cutting Detection Mesh property along five axes.

instance_conditioning.description: Instance-conditioning layer (type-level record): declares the layer, factors, escalate-only rule, demotion doctrine, raise guidance, inhibitors exclusion, binding contract, conditioning hints, status, and provenance. Fully typed in V1.6.

matrix_scope.description: Canonical scope sentence for a matrix, expressed in WHAT/WHY/WHERE terms. Defines the primary threat actor objective that places a tactic in this matrix at authoring time. Type-level field; not case-specific. See matrices.boundary_rule for the framework-vs-operational distinction.

phase_name.description: Human-readable phase name. Current data uses Title Case with phase number prefix (e.g., '1 Target Development'); V1.2 may normalize.

phase_4_track.description: Aftermath sub-track for phase-4 tactics: 'evasion' (Evade — withdrawal, evidence management, cover, counter-forensics, re-attack positioning) or 'attribution' (Claim — declaring, amplifying, messaging, coercive leverage). Framework-level structure carried by every matrix's phase-4 tactics; absent on phases 1–3. Formalized V1.3 (previously an undocumented data field on the People matrix).

notes.description: Formal taxonomic description of the tactic.

observed_contexts.description: Generic context archetypes (V1.1 mandatory). Pattern archetypes only; never case names.

evidence_basis.description: Declares the tactic's grounding (V1.1 mandatory). Machine-readable provenance.

source_refs.description: Bibliography keys. Min 1, with at least one Tier 1 source.

assessment_guidance.description: Optional structured per-tactic scoring guidance. Type-level inherent property of the tactic class; consumers cite the criteria preambles, high/low signal anchors, false-positive contexts, and threshold guidance to inform their own assessments. The criteria field on each of credibility/capability/intent/opportunity articulates the underlying judgment rule (e.g., 'Credibility rises with X, Y, Z; falls with A, B, C'); the high_signal_anchors and low_signal_anchors arrays illustrate the criteria with specific patterns and are indicative rather than exhaustive. Not a case-specific score. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

criteria.description: Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying credibility-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.

capability.description: Per-tactic aid for READING a specific actor's capability from evidence — the third of three deliberately distinct capability constructs: impact_potential presumes the class's capability ceiling; informs_axes.actor_capability scores what observing the class reveals about capability; this block guides the evidence reading. The per-case instance judgment is the future instance-conditioning record (B-03).

criteria.description: Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying capability-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.
Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying intent-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.
Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying opportunity-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.

false_positive_context.description: Patterns where surface behavior matches the tactic's indicators but the underlying activity is legitimate. Criteria + contexts shape mirrors the credibility/capability/intent/opportunity sub-fields.

criteria.description: Type-level prose articulating what distinguishes a false-positive from a real concern. Carries the contract; contexts illustrate it.

escalation_priority.description: Type-level priority class for the tactic — characterizes typical action-urgency at the tactic-class level, not case-level urgency at any specific assessment. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

target_identity_scope.description: Optional. Type-level declaration of which target_identity sub-classes this tactic's prose covers. Primarily meaningful for People matrix tactics. Authored per tactic based on actual prose coverage; tactics whose operational logic generalizes carry multiple values, tactics intrinsically narrow declare a single value. See target_identity on indicator for the per-indicator sub-dimension.

tactic_person.description: A tactic in the person matrix: the base tactic plus a matrix-specific id prefix and matrix const. Closes the wrong-matrix-placement class (F07/F08) in schema alone.

tactic_facility.description: A tactic in the facility matrix: base tactic plus TF id prefix and matrix const 'facility'.

tactic_organization.description: A tactic in the organization matrix: base tactic plus TO id prefix and matrix const 'organization'.

tactic_infrastructure.description: A tactic in the infrastructure matrix: base tactic plus TI id prefix and matrix const 'infrastructure'.

correlates_with.description: Indicator IDs this behavior co-occurs with (Detection Mesh cross-correlation). Referents are indicator IDs only, within or across matrices; cross-matrix links are inter-rater validated before authoring.

modality.description: Intrinsic modality of the behavior (V1.6 rename of 'crossing', restoring the locked S32 vocabulary), decided by the behavior's own mechanism, its INSTRUMENT, and the zone its access reaches; never its effect, target importance, or the venue it travels through. physical = matter, force, or presence is the instrument (kinetic/on-site/hand act); cyber = the instrument operates on a computing system's access, code, data, or machinery (a platform used merely as a communication channel does NOT qualify); cyber_physical = the behavior itself crosses the seam (a cyber action reaching/reading/writing the OT control plane, a physical implant gaining cyber reach, or a technical digital-or-electromagnetic means producing a physical-infrastructure effect); human_social = the instrument operates on people or institutions (persuasion, coercion, recruitment, legal or financial process) with no technical instrument, in which case the human_social boolean facet is necessarily true. CPN is NOT stored; it is computed over the Detection Mesh from crossings plus same-operation kill-chain membership.

crossing_mechanism.description: For modality=cyber_physical only: how the seam is crossed. digital = IT/network/software action reaches the OT control plane; electromagnetic = RF/GNSS/EW (jamming or spoofing of a signal a physical system depends on); physical_implant = a physical device placed to gain cyber reach.

human_social.description: Independent facet: true when the behavior's essence is influencing, recruiting, cultivating, coercing, deceiving, or negotiating with people, or is human warning-behavior leakage (grievance escalation, statements of intent, behavioral withdrawal), regardless of medium. Orthogonal to modality: a behavior may be human_social AND carry any modality value; a behavior whose modality IS human_social must carry human_social=true (schema-enforced).

temporal_signature.description: Type-level property of the indicator class describing how close to action it typically appears. Distinct from phase_relevance, which describes which lifecycle phase the indicator belongs to. Base values (horizon, advancing, imminent, staging, in_progress, aftermath) define primary pathway positions; optional _early / _late refinements are available for horizon, advancing, imminent, and aftermath where within-band variation carries meaningful operational signal. Staging and in_progress are not split (staging is already a tight terminal-prep window; in_progress is binary). Authors should use the base value when within-band position is ambiguous; use a granular variant only when the indicator class clearly clusters at the early or late edge of its band. Type-level inherent property; not case-specific. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

escalation_weight.description: Type-level composite over escalation_axes (0.0–10.0, two-decimal precision). Recommended derivation is published in escalation_rubric.composite_math; consumers may follow the recommendation or override with documented rationale. Type-level inherent property of the indicator class, not a case-specific score. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

escalation_axes.description: Type-level inherent properties of the indicator class along four axes. Sub-fields use _potential and _inverse suffixes deliberately, signalling that these describe the behavior class's typical implications, not case-level realizations at any specific facility or assessment. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

impact_potential.description: Type-level magnitude of harm the behavior class directly produces or imminently enables — a severity gradient along the pathway (reconnaissance/tradecraft low, planning/access mid, force application and capability acquisition high). Presumes the capability CEILING of the class (what it could effect at most); contrast informs_axes.actor_capability (what observing the class reveals about skill) and assessment_guidance.capability (how to read a specific actor's capability from evidence). The per-case does-THIS-actor-have-the-skill judgment belongs to the instance-conditioning layer (B-03) and is never discounted into this value.

blast_radius_potential.description: Type-level geographic / population scope if the threat lands.

recoverability_inverse.description: Type-level inverse-recoverability — how hard the harm is to undo. Permanence weighted higher; lives lost = highest. Reading election (rubric v1.2.0): this axis scores the harm the behavior class DIRECTLY produces — it does not inherit the permanence of the harm a behavior presages or enables (contrast impact_potential, which counts harm a behavior directly produces or imminently enables). Victim-facing pre-attack behaviors (surveillance, approach) score their durable psychological harm; operational support behaviors (rehearsal, diversion, coordination comms) score their own transient harm. Known seam: some phase-1/2 preparatory indicators were authored before this election under a presaged-harm reading and sit above it — reconciliation is a backlogged scoring pass (B-10), not silent per-indicator drift.

detectability.description: Type-level observability of the indicator in flight by trained personnel.

severity_band.description: Optional derived bucket from escalation_weight per escalation_rubric.severity_thresholds. Consumers may compute on read or store. Type-level descriptor of the indicator class. Note: when severity_floor is present, severity_band is the greater of the computed band and the floor (see escalation_rubric.severity_floor_rule). See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

severity_floor.description: V1.3 triage floor. Present on indicators whose behavior applies direct physical force to a person; forces severity_band to at least this value regardless of the computed escalation_weight (which is left unchanged). Currently 'critical' for all such behaviors — a casualty is critical at any scale. See escalation_rubric.severity_floor_rule.

axis_confidence.description: Optional per-axis evidence-basis marker (Ruling 10-A, V1.6): rule-derived by scripts/analysis/derive-axis-confidence.py, categorical only (numeric confidence is banned for the same false-precision reason informs_axes bans numbers). Confidence is evidence basis, NOT severity: a thin axis is a wider error bar and a candidate for earlier human review, NEVER an automatic demotion (a computed discount by the back door is banned per instance_conditioning). See escalation_rubric.axis_confidence_rubric for the derivation rules.

informs_axes.description: Type-level metadata describing which axes of the larger threat picture this indicator class typically informs, and how finely. Universal resolution scale (resolution, not severity — severity lives in escalation_axes): none = no signal on the axis; weak = resolves only the axis's coarsest grain (the axis-relevant fact exists); moderate = one grain finer (the coarse fact plus one narrowing); strong = resolves to a specific value. Rate the indicator class as written, type-level — never a vivid case instance. Six axes covering actor (capability / intent / opportunity) and the postulated event (timing / target / method). Categorical scale {strong, moderate, weak, none} — not numeric. The framework's collective judgment about how strongly an indicator class informs an axis is itself categorical at root; numeric values would be false precision. For AI/ML consumers needing continuous features, the documented mapping is strong=0.9, moderate=0.6, weak=0.3, none=0.0; this mapping is a downstream-consumer convention only, not framework-level scoring. Coverage: authored across all 815 indicator classes in all four matrices (People in V1.3; Facility, Infrastructure, and Organizations in V1.4–V1.5), each via a sealed-blind two-rater inter-rater process gated at weighted κ ≥ 0.60 per chunk; per-axis level semantics are formalized in each axis description (V1.3 refinements #1–#4). Field remains optional on any indicator. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

actor_capability.description: What observing the class REVEALS about the actor's skill, tradecraft, and operational sophistication — distinct from impact_potential (which presumes the class's capability ceiling) and from assessment_guidance.capability (a per-tactic aid for reading a specific actor's capability from evidence). Grains: none = purely passive/ambient behavior achievable with zero skill and zero deliberate effort (rare); weak = a deliberate action with no tradecraft visible; moderate = a real competence demonstrated (pretext durability, multi-modal coordination, concealed-imaging tradecraft, counter-surveillance); strong = advanced or specialized tradecraft (productive analysis of restricted artifacts, credential fabrication, manufacturing, regulatory-control defeat).

actor_intent.description: The actor's GENERAL intent-to-act, read at type level only — specific motive class is case-level and excluded. Grains: weak = diffuse or ambient adverse interest, not yet directed; moderate = purposive, directed attention toward the subject without clear commitment; strong = clear general intent-to-act (broad-to-narrow behavioral progression, operational specificity, retention of acquired materials, grievance paired with reconnaissance). Never raise to strong because a specific motive can be imagined. Formalizes V1.3 refinement #1.

actor_opportunity.description: The actor's opportunity, tiered rather than averaged across its two sub-meanings: weak = generic or ambient reach only; moderate = a resolved exploitable condition at the INFORMATIONAL tier (pattern-of-life knowledge, security-gap awareness); strong = REALIZED action-opportunity (an exploited insider relationship, direct unsupervised access, demonstrated reach within an exploitable window). During-execution support behaviors inherit the operation's realized opportunity (strong). Formalizes V1.3 refinement #2.

threat_timing.description: Proximity-to-action. Locked boundary: weak = phase-only (places the threat in a pathway phase with no finer resolution); moderate = phase plus something narrower (schedule-aligned behavior, operational-tempo cues); strong = pins a specific action window (imminent, dated, or event-aligned). Mobilization-phase rehearsal, probing, and attempted or actual breach/penetration behaviors read strong; concealment and OPSEC behaviors are excepted (weak).

threat_target.description: Which specific target or asset is in view. Grains: weak = targeting at a target-class level only; moderate = narrowed to a candidate set or subject-associated locations; strong = the specific named subject or subject-specific assets, including behaviors tied to a specific target-associated environment.

threat_method.description: How the attack would be conducted — the ATTACK method only: access and approach tradecraft does not inform method (reads none or weak). All execution in framework scope is physical; never treat physical-vs-digital as a narrowing (digital reconnaissance still describes a physical attack downstream). Grains: none = method-agnostic, all physical methods remain in play; weak = barely narrows the physical-methods space; moderate = narrows to 2–3 candidate physical methods; strong = pins a specific physical method (e.g., VBIED, hostage scenario, targeted assassination). Formalizes V1.3 refinement #3.

target_identity.description: Optional multi-select sub-dimension within the People matrix: the victim identity-class(es) this indicator class REVEALS (revealed reading — tag only what the behavior actually indicates; empty/absent = reveals nothing about victim identity). named_individual = one OR MORE specific pre-identified persons are the object — surveillance/profiling/approach/force/seizure/captivity/leverage directed at the person(s), OR a specific target-associated site/environment/route coupled to them (a site reveals that specific known person(s), singular or plural, are the target). role_or_identity_category = selection is by role/what-they-are (a judge, cops by uniform, clinic staff, journalists). affinity_group = a cohesive group property selects the victims (demographic, religious, ethnic — e.g. worshippers, a gathering). indiscriminate = anyone / random crowd, no selection filter (mass-casualty by proximity/availability). Empty/absent = the behavior class reveals nothing about victim identity (capability acquisition, breach/access mechanics, OPSEC/tradecraft, logistics, financing, evidence management, most aftermath evasion). Coupling rule: tag only when observing the class resolves WHO the victim is — the person(s) or their coupled site/environment; behaviors that merely presuppose a victim without revealing the class stay empty. Reproducibility validated by a sealed-blind spot-IRR (per-value Cohen κ 0.80). Replaces the prior compatibility reading, which tagged every class a behavior COULD serve and left the field near-constant at 179/190 all-four.

facility_target_scope.description: Optional Facility-matrix sub-dimension: the breadth of site selection this indicator class REVEALS about the actor (revealed reading — tag only what the behavior actually indicates, not what it could apply to; empty/absent = reveals nothing about breadth). specific_site = one identified building (grievance tied to a named facility, surveillance of a specific building, as-built drawings of this site). site_class = any facility of a FUNCTIONAL/OPERATIONAL type — grouped by what the site does (any branch of an org, any hospital, any transit hub, clinics/schools of a type). symbolic_category = any site of an IDEOLOGICALLY/SYMBOLICALLY-defined category — grouped by what the site represents (any government building, any place of worship of a faith, landmarks). The discriminator between site_class and symbolic_category is the BASIS OF GROUPING (function vs meaning), not specificity; both are breadth values (any member of the group). A single named site chosen for symbolic motive is specific_site, not symbolic_category. indiscriminate = any accessible site, opportunistic with no site preference. The Facility parallel to the People matrix `target_identity`; captures breadth (which/how many sites) distinct from blast_radius (how many victims) and informs_axes.threat_target (how well the indicator resolves the target). TARGET-COUPLING RULE: populate only when the behavior reveals the breadth of an ACTUAL target selection; general knowledge, capability, or method acquisition not coupled to a target or target-class carries no scope (empty). SYMBOLIC RULE: symbolic_category applies only when symbolism defines the target BREADTH (a category chosen for its meaning); symbolic MOTIVE for a named or class target does not make it symbolic_category — a specific building chosen for what it represents is specific_site. MULTI-TAG RULE: assign multiple values only when the behavior text explicitly spans breadths, or the observable behavior independently supports each — never because several possibilities can be inferred.

within_site_focus.description: Optional Facility-matrix sub-dimension: what inside the facility the indicator class REVEALS as the harm focus (revealed reading; empty/absent = unresolved). structure = the building/physical asset (arson, structural sabotage, defacement, demolition). occupants = the people inside (mass-casualty intent, hostage-taking, active-shooter positioning). systems = utilities/controls/functional systems whose defeat or contamination is the aim (power, water, HVAC/contamination, fire/security-system defeat that is the attack itself — NOT security-system defeat merely to gain access). whole_site = the site as an undifferentiated unit (seizure/occupation, generic threat against the facility). Decision rule for occupied-structure attacks: `occupants` when casualty intent is shown, `structure` when the aim is property/denial with incidental casualties, both only when the behavior genuinely reveals both aims. Facility-native (no People analog); load-bearing for triage. AIM-COUPLING RULE: populate only when the behavior reveals the within-site OBJECT OF HARM. Recon of site dimensions (floor plans, layout, security posture), method/capability acquisition (breaching tools, accelerants, ramming vehicles), and general technical literacy carry no focus (empty) unless explicitly coupled to a within-site aim. Floor-plan/layout study is recon, NOT a structure focus — reserve `structure` for load-bearing/collapse/destruction aims; reserve `systems` for utility/HVAC/fire-system defeat that is the attack itself.

primary_objective_evidence_tier.description: Optional. Incident-level annotation of the confidence with which the threat actor's primary objective (which sets matrix placement per matrices.boundary_rule) is established. stated = claimed responsibility or manifested intent. strongly_inferred = operational evidence overwhelming. weakly_inferred = operational evidence ambiguous. unknown = no basis for inference; matrix placement defaults to the matrix containing the tactic that produced the most observable consequence (see matrices.boundary_rule). As of schema 2.1.0 the canonical home for this incident-level annotation is $defs.conditioned_assessment.primary_objective_evidence_tier, which is where a case consumer writes it and which adds a 'contested' value for disputed hostile-actor existence; this type-level field is retained for compatibility and is not populated on shipped indicators. Full IRR protocol for this field is deferred to a future release.

conditioning_guidance.description: Framework-provided default investigative-tasking guidance for conditioning this indicator at instance time: which instance factors to probe (probe_factors, machine-filterable) and a natural-language directive (guidance). Assessment-scoped only: immediate response actions (alerting, notification, mitigation) are carried by the tactic's response_protocols, never by this field. A starting point, NOT a complete or prescriptive instruction: consumers may follow, extend, or override it with their own playbooks (as with escalation_rubric). Intended for composition across combinations of observed indicators (see detection_mesh / correlates_with), not single-indicator reading. Type-level; does not affect the score.

probe_factors.description: Machine-readable index of the instance factors this indicator's guidance points at. Enum names match $defs.instance_assessment's six factors.

guidance.description: Natural-language practitioner directive: what to go collect and why it decides how dangerous the case is. No em or en dashes (enforced by pattern).

compensates_for.description: Countermeasure-to-countermeasure compensation: this countermeasure compensates for the ABSENCE or failure of the referenced countermeasure (redundancy relation). Indicator coverage does NOT live here; it lives in mitigates. An IND- referent in this field is a type error.

function.description: How this countermeasure acts on the behavior's pathway: prevent (stops the act), detect (surfaces the act), deny (removes the act's value). Authored per edge, never inherited from the countermeasure. 'unreviewed' is a provisional value for migrated legacy edges pending review; it must reach zero before the coverage layer ships, and a detect-only edge caps coverage at partial.

mitigates.description: The countermeasure-to-indicator mitigation relation: this countermeasure prevents, detects, or denies the referenced behavior, per the ratified linking criterion (acts on the behavior's pathway; same-tactic membership is not sufficient; cross-tactic edges are expected where a countermeasure genuinely reaches). This is the coverage-derivation input, the scored indicator-level coverage relation committed by the earlier transitional note.

target_identity.description: Optional. Mirror of indicator target_identity for the small set of person-matrix countermeasures whose coverage is scoped by victim identity-class. Present on 4 countermeasures; same enum and multi-select semantics as indicator.target_identity.

coordinates_with.description: Response-protocol IDs that co-activate on overlapping indicator sets (Detection Mesh co-activation). A directed dependency layer (gates / precedes / deconflicts) is the committed evolution of this relation.

category_label.description: Human-readable label for the actor category.

awareness.description: Whether the actor is aware of / intends the threat activity (e.g. witting vs unwitting).

direction.description: Directionality of the actor relative to the protected entity (e.g. internal vs external).

access_relationship.description: The actor's access relationship to the target (insider access, trusted third party, outsider, etc.).

phase_compression_risk.description: Type-level note on this actor class's tendency to compress the attack lifecycle phases.

actor_level.description: Sophistication / resourcing tier of the actor class.

attack_vectors.description: Attack vectors typically available to this actor class.

primary_matrices.description: Target matrices this actor class primarily operates against.

behavioral_markers.description: Observable behavioral markers characteristic of this actor class.

ai_enabled_risks.description: AI-specific risk amplifiers applicable to this actor class (may be empty). See ai_architecture.vectors.ai_enabled_risks.

v2_tactic_associations.description: Reserved for V2 tactic associations; currently an empty array on every profile.

insider_type.description: Optional. Present on insider actor classes (e.g. malicious / negligent / compromised).

insider_subtype.description: Optional. Finer insider classification (e.g. recruited / coerced / unwitting).

employment_status.description: Optional. Employment status of the insider actor class (e.g. current).

state_actor_type.description: Optional. Present on state-actor classes (e.g. direct / proxy / front / sponsored).

matrices.description: Optional. Which target matrices this source supports/informs. Enables consumers to pull sourcing by matrix and the UI to group the bibliography by matrix. A source may support multiple matrices; tagging (not partitioning) keeps flat key-based citation intact.

topics.description: Optional. Attack-method / subject tags for filtering sources by need (e.g., bombing, arson, structural_sabotage, forced_entry, vehicle_ramming, soft_targets, target_selection, cbrn_contamination, cyber_physical, building_systems_sabotage, occupation_siege, symbolic_ideological, active_shooter, insider_threat, mass_attack, threat_assessment, protective_intelligence, risk_methodology, physical_protection_systems, incident_data, financial_crime). Free-string to allow extension; the listed vocabulary is the recommended starter set.

instance_assessment.description: Layer 2 — a per-CASE instance-conditioning record for a specific assessment of a specific actor and target, SEPARATE from the type-level indicator score. The framework defines this contract but ships NO instances (it is a type-level artifact; consumers instantiate per case). Records discrete observations, never optional prose, and never a computed capability discount. See the top-level instance_conditioning block for the escalate-only rule and binding contract.

target_focus.description: Directionality of the observed behavior toward a target: diffuse (no resolved target) → narrowing (candidate set or associated locus) → specific_target (a specific subject/asset resolved). unknown when not assessable.

pathway_stage.description: This actor's assessed position on the pathway to violence (NTAC / phase_mappings vocabulary) — the CASE stage, which may lead or lag the indicator class's type-level phase.

means_in_hand.description: Whether THIS actor actually has the capability/means now — the honest per-case capability cell. unknown is the default and must NOT lower priority (absence of evidence is not evidence of absence; capability is volatile and easy to be wrong about). Used to ESCALATE when present, never to discount.

tempo_trajectory.description: Direction and rate of the actor's movement along the pathway across observations.

proximity_access.description: The actor's access state relative to the target — a STATE, not a stage: an insider has access without ever breaching, and folding access into pathway_stage conflates having access with seeking it. unknown is the safe default and must NOT lower priority (same doctrine as means_in_hand). Used to ESCALATE when attained, never to discount. Ruling Q3a, 2026-07-28 session.

source_credibility.description: Reliability of the reporting behind this record — conditions how much weight the other five factors carry. In an escalate-only system it functions as a brake on raising, never a scaler down: a low-credibility screaming instance cannot be dismissed (the type floor holds) and cannot stampede the queue (the raise waits for corroboration). Ruling Q4, 2026-07-28 session.

basis.description: Optional free-text evidentiary basis or analyst note.

conditioned_assessment.description: The binding object (B-04): a type-level indicator score CONDITIONED by an instance record. A type score becomes a case assessment only when joined to its instance record — this object requires BOTH, so a consumer cannot emit a conditioned assessment from the bare number. Escalate-only: conditioned_priority may raise priority above the type band but never lower it below (the false-LOW is the deadly error; a silent capability discount is forbidden). Whether the instance HELD or RAISED the band is not stored: it is derived by comparing conditioned_priority to type_severity_band (raised iff conditioned_priority > type_severity_band), the same base-vs-environmental comparison CVSS uses; storing it would duplicate state that can drift. Raise decisions follow the advisory instance_conditioning.raise_guidance patterns; de-prioritization is a case-management disposition and is never written back into the score (instance_conditioning.demotion_doctrine).

indicator_id.description: Reference to the type-level indicator whose score is being conditioned.

type_severity_band.description: The indicator's type-level severity_band — the FLOOR. conditioned_priority is never below this.

conditioned_priority.description: The resulting triage priority, always >= type_severity_band (escalate-only invariant). The floor is enforced structurally by the conditional subschemas on this object: for a correctly stated type_severity_band, a below-floor conditioned_priority fails validation. The one obligation schema cannot enforce is band fidelity, that type_severity_band equals the authored severity_band of indicator_id at a stated framework version; that join is owned by the reference validator and the consumer SDK. The held-vs-raised distinction is derived from this field against type_severity_band; there is deliberately no stored effect flag and no representable downward move.

primary_objective_evidence_tier.description: Optional incident-level confidence that the threat actor's primary objective, and therefore the primary-matrix placement, is correctly identified. This is the incident-level home the boundary_rule annotation refers to. 'stated' the objective is explicit; 'strongly_inferred' and 'weakly_inferred' inferred from behavior; 'contested' the evidence conflicts or the existence of a hostile actor is itself disputed (distinct from 'unknown', which is no basis for inference).

disposition.description: Optional case-management outcome recorded ALONGSIDE the score, never written back into it (instance_conditioning.demotion_doctrine). A benign reassessment exits as 'closed_benign' and a disrupted plot as 'disrupted_by_interdiction' without lowering conditioned_priority: the disposition, not a score rewrite, carries the outcome.
